problem: Signals of progress in AI/ML peer review are fragmented across venues with different rules and formats, making it hard to track trends and key moments like rebuttals and decisions.
approach: Paper Copilot pulls peer-review data from official sites, OpenReview, and opt-in forms into a single standardized, versioned archive with timestamps, enabling consistent cross-venue analysis.
contribution: Demonstrates on ICLR 2024/2025 that larger score changes occur after rebuttal for higher-tier papers and that 2025 shows sharper, mean-score-driven tier assignment with lower decision uncertainty.

problem: Cross-entropy loss in standard LLM fine-tuning forces one-hot target distributions and ignores alternative valid continuations, limiting output diversity needed for generative applications.
approach: Training with Sparsemax+ applies a suppression term to penalize out-of-support probabilities, while testing with softmax maintains calibrated, non-degenerate probability distributions for diverse samples.
contribution: Improves accuracy and output diversity on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen-2.5-7B across chat, code, and open-domain benchmarks as a drop-in fine-tuning solution.

problem: Existing all-in-one image restoration methods handle only specific domains; extending to multiple domains (natural, medical, remote sensing) requires a unified approach that balances domain-specific and cross-domain knowledge.
approach: DATPRL-IR constructs task and domain prompt pools from multimodal LLMs, adaptively selects and composes prompts via a prompt composition mechanism to fuse domain-aware and task-specific representations.
contribution: First multi-domain all-in-one image restoration method that outperforms SOTA methods while showing strong generalization across domains.

problem: Language models' ability to categorize sentences by modality (possible, impossible, nonsensical) has been questioned, yet the mechanisms for modal categorization remain unclear.
approach: Uses mechanistic interpretability techniques to identify linear modal difference vectors in LM activations and correlates projections along these vectors with human judgments of event plausibility.
contribution: Shows LMs have more reliable modal categorization than previously reported and identifies a consistent emergence order of modal representations through training steps, layers, and model capacity.

problem: The interaction between positional and semantic information in Transformers is insufficiently explored; mainstream methods obscure this relationship and hinder systematic comparative studies.
approach: Deconstructs attention-logit computation, analyzes all mainstream positional encodings on synthetic tasks that explicitly demand positional-semantic synthesis, focusing on RoPE's product-based structure.
contribution: Identifies RoPE's advantage on tasks requiring strong positional-semantic synthesis and uncovers a hidden training bias called the single-head deposit pattern in shallow layers.

problem: Standard RoPE implementations discard the imaginary component of complex-valued dot products, losing phase information crucial for modeling long-context dependencies.
approach: Extends RoPE to leverage the full complex-valued representation by re-incorporating the imaginary component into a dual-component attention score.
contribution: Improves long-context language modeling performance over standard RoPE, with benefits scaling with context length, on multiple long-context benchmarks.

problem: High-quality image synthesis requires efficient latent representations; product quantization is underutilized for generative models despite its classical scalability advantages.
approach: PQGAN integrates product quantization into VQGAN's vector quantization framework, analyzing interactions between codebook size, embedding dimensionality, and subspace factorization.
contribution: Achieves PSNR of 37dB (prior work 27dB) and reduces FID, LPIPS, CMMD by up to 96%; integrates seamlessly into pretrained diffusion models for faster generation or doubled resolution.

problem: Citations generated by standalone LLMs are unreliable due to hallucinations; existing systems rely on test-time retrieval, introducing latency and infrastructure dependence.
approach: Active Indexing augments continual pretraining with synthetic data that restates facts in diverse forms and enforces bidirectional training (source-to-fact and fact-to-source) to bind facts to document identifiers.
contribution: Achieves citation accuracy of 95.2% with only 3.5% human involvement on CitePretrainBench, enabling retrieval-free knowledge attribution without test-time retrieval.

problem: MoE models incur prohibitive memory costs due to duplicate expert parameters; existing per-expert compression methods overlook structural redundancies across experts.
approach: TD-MoE jointly factorizes expert weights via cross-expert tensorization with 3D decomposition, multi-linear whitening, and dynamic rank allocation to balance compression and reconstruction error.
contribution: Achieves 20% parameter reduction with near-lossless performance and 11-14% gains over decomposition baselines at 40-60% compression on Qwen2-57B and Mixtral-8x7B.

problem: Post-training quantization for visual autoregressive models faces large reconstruction errors in attention-value products and misalignment between codebook sampling frequencies and predicted probabilities.
approach: Shift-and-sum quantization reduces errors by aggregating results from symmetrically shifted value tokens; resampling strategy aligns codebook entry frequencies with predicted probabilities.
contribution: Establishes SOTA in PTQ for VAR across class-conditional generation, in-painting, out-painting, and editing tasks with consistent improvements.

problem: LLM-based recommenders struggle in continual learning as users and preferences evolve; existing LoRA-based methods over-emphasize preserving past task performance, ignoring that outdated preferences harm current performance.
approach: PESO applies a proximal regularizer anchoring the current LoRA adapter to its recent frozen state, enabling flexible balance between adaptation and preservation of recent behaviors.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing LoRA-based continual learning methods with data-aware, direction-wise guidance in the LoRA subspace.

problem: Visual place recognition requires robust geotagged image retrieval despite large appearance and viewpoint variation; existing methods neglect dynamic spatial-visual interplay during training.
approach: SAGE jointly improves local feature aggregation, training sample organization, and hard sample mining via a soft probing module and online geo-visual graph that fuses geographic proximity and visual similarity.
contribution: Achieves SOTA across eight benchmarks; notably 100% Recall@10 on SPED using only 4096D descriptors with frozen DINOv2 and parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

problem: IR benchmark evaluation is hindered by incomplete labeling with unlabeled relevant chunks and unreliable LLM assessments; existing systems suffer from LLM overconfidence and poor escalation to humans.
approach: DREAM employs multi-round debate between LLM agents with opposing initial stances and iterative reciprocal critique; agreement-based debate handles certain cases while escalating uncertain ones to humans.
contribution: Achieves 95.2% labeling accuracy with only 3.5% human involvement and identifies 29,824 missing relevant chunks, showing that unlabeled data distorts retriever rankings.

problem: Sleep analysis traditionally relies on standard devices (PSG, bedside monitors, wearables) that capture heterogeneous biosignals; device differences and sensor dropout hinder unified modeling.
approach: sleep2vec is a foundation model that learns shared representations via cross-modal contrastive pretraining on 42,249 recordings using a physiology-aware InfoNCE objective that dynamically weights negatives.
contribution: Outperforms baselines on sleep staging and clinical outcomes while remaining robust to any modality subset and sensor dropout; characterizes scaling laws for nocturnal biosignals.

problem: Multimodal LLMs for spatial tasks ignore camera parameters, entangling object properties with camera perspective and leading to overfitting to training camera distributions rather than learning generalizable 3D geometry.
approach: Camera-Aware MLLM injects camera intrinsics via dense embeddings per visual token, applies camera-aware data augmentation to vary parameters, and distills geometric priors from 3D vision models.
contribution: Substantially outperforms naive MLLMs on cross-camera generalization tests, demonstrating that camera-awareness is prerequisite for robust spatial reasoning.

problem: Tool-augmented LLMs often show systematic bias in selecting functionally equivalent tools, privileging some providers while disadvantaging others, compromising fairness.
approach: Benchmarks tool selection bias across diverse categories; experiments reveal semantic alignment, description perturbations, and pre-training exposure as key factors; proposes filtering-then-uniform-sampling mitigation.
contribution: Identifies unfairness as critical deployment obstacle and demonstrates that text-based safety alignment partially transfers to multimodal domains.

problem: Native VLMs (unified pixel-to-word architectures) face fundamental constraints in aligning representations and integrating vision-language strengths compared to modular VLMs.
approach: NEO builds native VLMs from first principles with three design criteria: effective pixel-word alignment, seamless module integration, and unified cross-modal encoding; trained on 390M image-text examples.
contribution: Narrows gap with top-tier modular counterparts across diverse scenarios while providing reusable components for scalable native VLM development.

problem: Vision language models are strongly biased by knowledge of popular subjects, causing systematic failures on objective visual tasks like counting and identification.
approach: Tests VLMs on counting tasks across diverse domains (animals, logos, chess, optical illusions) and analyzes reasoning patterns; background removal and thinking-token analysis reveal overthinking phenomenon.
contribution: Shows VLMs score 17.05% on counting tasks; background removal improves to 21.09%; reasoning accuracy initially rises to 40% then declines with overthinking.

problem: Understanding human cognition and behavior requires integrating multiple modalities; existing methods lack large-scale synchronized datasets of egocentric vision and brain activity.
approach: EgoBrain dataset synchronizes 32-channel EEG and first-person video over 61 hours from 40 participants across 29 activity categories; develops multimodal fusion framework for action understanding.
contribution: Achieves 66.70% action recognition accuracy; dataset of 61 hours enables cross-subject and cross-environment validation with open science sharing.

problem: Creating realistic humanoid character animations requires significant time and cost; synthesizing 4D animations directly from static models is underexplored.
approach: Uses generative video models to synthesize 4D animated sequences from static 3D meshes and text prompts via rendered image conditioning and SMPL-based motion optimization.
contribution: Enables cost-effective synthesis of diverse and realistic humanoid animations guided by video model motion priors.

problem: Large Audio Language Models are vulnerable to jailbreak attacks; safety of LALMs with audio modalities remains largely unexplored due to lack of adversarial datasets and unified evaluation frameworks.
approach: JALMBench includes 11,316 text and 245,355 audio samples, supports 12 LALMs, 8 attack methods, and 5 defense methods; provides in-depth analysis of attack efficiency, topic sensitivity, and architecture.
contribution: Finds LALM safety strongly influenced by modality and architecture; text-based safety partially transfers to audio; interleaving audio-text enables cross-modal generalization.

problem: LLMs face critical challenge of remaining safe against jailbreak attacks while maintaining general reasoning capabilities.
approach: Answer-Then-Check uses thinking ability to evaluate safety before generating final answers; trains on ReSA dataset of 80K examples teaching reasoning and safety analysis.
contribution: Achieves Pareto frontier with superior safety and lower over-refusal while maintaining reasoning on MMLU, MATH500, HumanEval; enables safe completion with helpful alternatives.

problem: Most egocentric vision benchmarks focus on daytime scenarios; low-light conditions inevitable in real-world applications remain largely unexplored.
approach: EgoNight introduces day-night aligned videos using synthetic Blender rendering and real recordings to enhance nighttime annotation quality; auto-labeling engine with human verification creates EgoNight-VQA benchmark.
contribution: Constructs 3658 QA pairs across 90 videos spanning 12 VQA types with day-night alignment; reveals substantial performance drops from day to night, underscoring low-light reasoning challenges.

problem: 3D single object tracking must capture both spatial shape and temporal motion features while generalizing across object categories; existing category-specific methods sacrifice generalizability.
approach: PointRePar captures latent point relations across spatial and temporal domains via Mamba-based U-Net for multi-scale relations and box-level temporal relations for motion features.
contribution: Outperforms category-unified and category-specific SOTA methods across three benchmarks while enabling joint training across multiple categories.

problem: Vision-language models lack fundamental capability of visual verification and refinement during reasoning and generation; existing VLMs underperform on critical visual verification tasks.
approach: Builds ViVerBench spanning 16 verification task categories; trains OmniVerifier-7B on automated pipelines; proposes OmniVerifier-TTS for test-time scaling via iterative fine-grained optimization.
contribution: Demonstrates three atomic capabilities in visual verification that generalize synergistically; achieves +8.3 on ViVerBench, +3.7 on T2I-ReasonBench, +4.3 on GenEval++.

problem: Conditional image generation struggles to harmonize conflicting guidance from text and conditioning inputs: input-level conflicts where semantics contradict, and model-bias conflicts where learned biases hinder alignment.
approach: BideDPO constructs two disentangled preference pairs (one per constraint) to mitigate gradient entanglement; automated pipeline generates conflict-aware data; adaptive loss balancing manages pair influence.
contribution: Enables nuanced case-by-case trade-offs for multi-constraint image generation via bidirectionally decoupled DPO with iterative optimization.

problem: Pathology image segmentation must generalize to out-of-domain tissue morphologies and novel pathologies; existing reasoning segmentation methods lack pathology-specific knowledge and proper segmentation timing.
approach: PathChat-SegR1 combines pathology-specific vision encoders with stain-invariant self-distillation; proposes SO-GRPO to learn optimal segmentation timing based on accumulated reasoning context.
contribution: Achieves 61% improvement over SOTA on out-of-domain pathology images using reasoning-based segmentation on pathology-specific benchmark of 118,667 triplets.

problem: Sparse autoencoders fail to fully recover ground-truth monosemantic features from superposed polysemantic ones unless features are extremely sparse; limiting conditions remain theoretically unclear.
approach: Provides first theoretical analysis with closed-form solution; proposes reweighting strategy targeting ground-truth monosemantic reconstruction; establishes weight selection principle for weighted SAE.
contribution: Reveals fundamental SAE limitations theoretically and demonstrates that reweighting significantly improves feature monosemanticity and interpretability.

problem: CLIP vision encoder has notable limitations: fixed input resolution handling and failure to separate embeddings for dissimilar images; replacing it typically requires full model retraining.
approach: QLIP replaces CLIP with content-aware quadtree-based patchification addressing mesoscopic and interpolation biases; integrates via few lines of code without retraining.
contribution: Improves LLaVA visual QA across model sizes without retraining; boosts V* benchmark by up to 13.6%.

problem: LLM agent benchmarks focus on reasoning, planning, and execution while under-evaluating memory encompassing memorization, updating, and retrieval of long-term information.
approach: MemoryAgentBench transforms existing datasets into multi-turn format simulating incremental information processing; covers four core competencies: accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding, selective forgetting.
contribution: Provides comprehensive testbed for memory agents across four competencies with multi-turn interactive format reflecting agent behavior.

problem: Visual geometry reconstruction typically anchors to designated reference views, introducing inductive bias that causes instability and failures if the reference is suboptimal.
approach: π³ employs fully permutation-equivariant architecture to predict affine-invariant poses and scale-invariant local point maps without reference frames.
contribution: Achieves SOTA on camera pose, depth, and dense point map reconstruction tasks while maintaining robustness to input ordering.

problem: MAP inference in credal networks with imprecise probabilities is computationally harder than in Bayesian networks due to complex joint credal set operations.
approach: Develops depth-first branch-and-bound search algorithms for maximax and maximin MAP tasks; exploits problem decomposition via AND/OR search space with partitioning-based heuristics.
contribution: Provides exact algorithms for credal network MAP inference that scale to large and complex instances using effective heuristic guidance.

problem: Contrastive learning under imbalanced data degrades representation quality and induces bias, yet rigorous theoretical characterization of these effects is lacking.
approach: Develops theoretical framework analyzing training dynamics of Transformer-based contrastive learning under imbalance; reveals three-stage weight evolution; proposes pruning to restore performance.
contribution: Shows minority features reduce capacity and hinder ground-truth separation; demonstrates pruning restores performance degraded by imbalance with both theoretical and empirical validation.

problem: Reasoning in audio LLMs shows test-time inverse scaling where longer chains degrade performance; models lack proper training for consistent reasoning.
approach: CESAR employs Group Relative Policy Optimization with multi-faceted reward suite incentivizing correctness, consistency, structured patterns, causal reasoning, domain knowledge, and calibrated depth.
contribution: Resolves test-time inverse scaling and achieves SOTA on MMAU Test-mini and near-human performance on MMSU, outperforming Gemini 2.5 Pro and GPT-4o Audio.

problem: Logic synthesis must balance compact circuit generation with functional accuracy; existing methods struggle with this trade-off, often yielding suboptimal circuits.
approach: CircuitEvo models circuits as structured programs and iteratively leverages LLMs guided by domain-specific evolutionary prompts; structure-aware optimization corrects functional discrepancies.
contribution: Achieves up to 16 inputs and 69 outputs; significantly outperforms SOTA methods with 6.74% average circuit size improvement; first LLM-based LS approach enabling iterative compactness improvement.

problem: Video query sound separation struggles with homogeneous interference and overlapping soundtracks due to limited temporal modeling and weak audiovisual alignment.
approach: AlignSep uses flow matching with temporal consistency mechanisms guiding the vector field toward robust audiovisual alignment; addresses multi-conditioned generation challenges unique to VQSS.
contribution: Achieves SOTA on multiple benchmarks; introduces VGGSound-Hard benchmark; demonstrates practical value for real-world separation in complex scenes.

problem: Portrait synthesis must preserve fine-grained facial details of reference identity while maintaining strong text alignment; single-stream methods fail to capture and guide fine-grained details.
approach: OmniPortrait introduces pivotal optimization with Pivot ID Encoder trained via face localization and Reference-Based Guidance performing on-the-fly feature matching over diffusion features.
contribution: Demonstrates significant improvements in identity preservation and text alignment; naturally generalizes to multi-identity customization scenarios.

problem: Converting attention modules like grouped-query attention to multi-head latent attention can improve expressivity without KV-cache cost, but naive SVD conversion causes activation drift and degraded attention fidelity.
approach: CARE introduces activation-preserving factorization aligned with actual activations, adjusted-rank allocation distributing fixed KV budget to layers needing it most, and KV-parity mapping.
contribution: Delivers up to 331% relative gains over uniform-rank SVD on Llama-3-8B; fully recovers original accuracy with brief post-SVD healing fine-tune.

problem: Large multimodal models incur substantial computational and memory costs hindering deployment; existing methods decouple low-rank decomposition and quantization, compounding errors.
approach: LLaVA-FA performs joint low-rank plus quantization in the frequency domain; introduces PolarQuant for complex matrices and optional diagonal calibration eliminating large-scale data needs.
contribution: Outperforms existing efficient multimodal models while maintaining minimal activated parameters and low computational costs.

problem: Fine-tuning diffusion models via policy gradient methods requires intractable marginal likelihoods; existing methods use alternative proposals and relaxations.
approach: Unifies RAFT variants as GRAFT with same PPO solution but reshaped rewards; introduces P-GRAFT to shape intermediate noise levels; proposes inverse noise correction for flow models.
contribution: Improves Stable Diffusion 2 on T2I with 8.81% relative gain over base; shows inverse noise correction improves FID on unconditional generation with lower FLOPs.
